articles.title: Dan Campbell Responds to Sam LaPorta's Explosive Comments About Lions Contract Talks
articles.summary: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell defended Sam LaPorta after the star tight end said he would consider playing elsewhere next season amid stalled extension negotiations.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell defended Sam LaPorta after the star tight end said he would consider playing elsewhere next season amid stalled extension negotiations.

Campbell told reporters LaPorta is "locked in" despite his comments ahead of the Lions' upcoming Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers this Sunday.

"Look, I've said things that I regret... that doesn't mean that's who the person is," Campbell said Friday. "You say something, it's— sometimes you get something off your chest. But we pick the guys we pick for a reason, because we know their character, and we know that they're about deep down.

"Sam's a stud, alright? And he's going to help us win games. And he really is, he's an unselfish teammate, an unselfish player."

LaPorta said in a recent appearance on Pardon My Take he would "go get paid somewhere else" if he and the Lions weren't able to reach resolution on an extension.

"I break my f--king back for the team, and then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love," LaPorta said.

LaPorta underwent surgery on a herniated disc in his back last November. He has made 37 catches for 316 receiving yards and three touchdowns in his first five games back since the procedure.

Campbell said LaPorta's comments hadn't been a "distraction" in the Lions locker room since the podcast aired.

"You can never take anything personal when you start talking about business. That's why business and football, they don't belong with each other," Campbell said.

Campbell then showed frustration after more questions regarding LaPorta, at which point he told a reporter, "I said I didn't want it to be a distraction, and now it's becoming one, because you keep asking these things."

LaPorta is playing the season in the final year of his rookie deal. ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported earlier this month he and the Lions had paused contract talks.

The Lions do not have a policy again in-season contract talks, but Rapoport noted at the time "the thought is that a deal is unlikely considering the two sides couldn't reach an agreement over the first four weeks of the season."

The tight end market is currently led by the San Francisco 49ers' George Kittle, Arizona Cardinals' Trey McBride and Green Bay Packers' Tucker Kraft who each make in the neighborhood of $19 million per season. Rapoport previously reported he could see LaPorta potentially resetting the positional market when he signs his next deal.

articles.title: Donald Trump: US President says NFL Paris game on Sunday 'could have been postponed' amid civil unrest
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the New Orleans Saints in Paris - live on Sky Sports NFL from 1pm, Sunday (kick-off, 1.30pm); the French government are deploying a larger security presence in the city following a week of civil unrest, with further demonstrations planned
articles.body:
France is bracing for more demonstrations Saturday against the high cost of living, with museums closing and the government deploying a larger security presence to prevent a repeat of last week's violent unrest.

The game on Sunday - the first ever NFL regular-season game held in France - is taking place at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just north of the capital.

"I think maybe it's looking like tomorrow is going to be a bad day in France, so you worry about it," Trump told reporters.

"I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match, because France is really in trouble."

The US State Department issued a security alert late on Thursday, saying: "Numerous groups submitted plans for protests on Saturday October 24. Americans in Paris for the NFL game on Sunday October 25, should also exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings.

"While permits may be filed for demonstration routes, last-minute changes can happen and protests can occur outside planned routes."

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said this week that preparations were made in consultation with US and French authorities.

Street protests, he said, "are not unusual in France". The league did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump's remarks.

Soccer team Paris Saint-Germain's game against Lyon has been moved from Sunday to Monday evening at the request of Paris police.

The game was scheduled for Sunday night in Parc des Princes.

Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said on Friday that "the NFL is alert to what's going on".

He added: "This game means a lot to the NFL. If it was unsafe, then I'm sure we wouldn't be here."

A weekend event for Steelers fans was cancelled on Thursday because of security concerns.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson, Puka Nacua, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 7
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson's status for Week 7 is still under evaluation.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson's status for Week 7 is still under evaluation.

The Baltimore Ravens quarterback, who missed the last two weeks with an ankle injury, was practiced on Friday and said he's improving ahead of Sunday's AFC North battle with the Cincinnati Bengals

Puka Nacua contains a similar status for Sunday after he left Los Angeles Rams practice on Thursday with a calf issue. Nacua didn't suffer a long-term injury, but there are concerns about whether he'll be able to play in Week 7 or not.

Below is a look at all of the significant injury news affecting fantasy football matchups in Week 7.

Lamar Jackson's Status Yet To Be Determined

The Ravens have yet to rule Lamar Jackson out of Sunday's clash with the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jackson, who revealed on Friday that he's been dealing with a high ankle sprain, said he's "heading in the right direction" for Sunday, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wouldn't commit either way on Jackson's status when he addressed the media on Friday.

The Ravens posted a 1-1 record without Jackson so far this season. Tyler Huntley led them to an overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons. They then lost to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

If Jackson plays, the assumption would be that he doesn't run as much to put more pressure on the ankle. He may be more inclined to sit back in the pocket and throw, or rely more on Derrick Henry to carry the offensive load.

The Bengals allowed over 300 total yards in four of their first five games. They let up over 100 rushing yards in their three games prior to their Week 6 bye.

It's an ideal matchup for Henry, regardless of who the quarterback is, but if Jackson plays, the forecast for the Baltimore pass-catchers is better.

Jackson passed for over 200 yards in three of his four starts. He completed 75 percent of his passes in his last two games before the injury.

Huntley threw for 366 yards in the last two weeks. He was better against Atlanta and struggled a bit against Cleveland in a tougher matchup.

Huntley is a solid replacement for Jackson in fantasy football, if he starts for a third straight week. The matchup against Cincinnati should allow Huntley to put up a similar stat line to the Atlanta game.

Regardless of quarterback, the best waiver-wire move involving a Ravens player is picking up tight end Josh Cuevas. The rookie out of Alabama scored last week and had six catches on seven targets in the last two weeks.

Puka Nacua Listed As Questionable, Does Not Practice Friday

Puka Nacua is officially listed as questionable for the Rams' Week 7 battle with the Las Vegas Raiders.

Nacua left practice on Thursday with a calf issue. That ailment kept him out of practice on Friday.

Nacua's potential absence would be a massive blow to the Rams offense, a unit that is already without Davante Adams for an extended period of time.

Matthew Stafford's fantasy value would crater if Nacua and Adams, arguably the best wide receiver tandem in the NFL, aren't on the field.

Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington are next up on the wide receiver depth chart for the Rams.

However, it might be smarter to go with Blake Corum, Tyler Higbee or Colby Parkinson

The Rams utilize a good amount of multi-tight end sets and they have two solid pass-catching running backs in Corum and Kyren Williams.

The Denver Broncos are a team to target, if you want to pivot away from the Rams as a whole.

Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle haven't had great starts, but they're facing an Arizona Cardinals defense that's given up the second-most touchdowns to wide receivers.

San Francisco's Brandin Cooks is worth a waiver-wire look because of his expanded role in the 49ers offense due to injuries. He's also facing an Atlanta defense that's allowed the most receptions to opposing wide outs.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Form Union in Historic Move, NFL Team Agrees to Recognize DCCA
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have agreed to recognize the newly-formed union of their cheerleading squad.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have agreed to recognize the newly-formed union of their cheerleading squad.

Per a release from the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders Association, the NFL organization agreed to recognize the DCCA as the collective bargaining representative for the cheerleading squad.

Schottenheimer 'Pissed Off' by Cowboys Start

The move makes the Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders the first known squad for an NFL team to unionize.

The Cowboys cheerleaders are among the most well-known dance groups in the United States. They have been featured in the Netflix series America's Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders that released its third season in June.

In the second season of the show (h/t Angelique Jackson of Variety ), Megan McElaney revealed in the final episode that a veteran group of the cheerleaders reached out to Cowboys officials to negotiate new contracts.

"We ended up getting a 400% increase, which is, like, life-changing," McElaney said.

McElaney has since retired from the Cowboys cheerleading squad after five seasons.

A 2022 report from Kristen Conti of NBC Sports Boston noted they earn between $15-20 per hour and around $75,000 annually. That amount would have been before the pay increase McElaney spoke about.

The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders were established in 1961, one year after the team's inaugural season. Their squad is comprised of 36 members with Kelli Finglass serving as director and Judy Tramell serving as choreographer.

articles.title: France's top soccer team obeys police order to move Sunday match; Saints, Steelers owners meet with Macron
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain postponed its match under police orders, but the NFL's New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers game remains on schedule.
articles.body: It may be starting to get redundant but, "Yes," the NFL game between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers remains on track, a league spokesman told OutKick and Fox News Digital on Friday. The question came up – again – because the most successful soccer team in France on Friday announced it has postponed its match on Sunday in Paris under police orders. Paris-Saint Germain issued a statement that said it has "taken note" of the order from the Paris Police Prefecture prohibiting the organization of the Paris Saint-Germain-Olympique Lyonnais match. STEELERS CANCEL PARIS FAN EVENT OVER FEARS OF UNREST WHILE NFL PUSHES AHEAD WITH ITS OWN EVENT AND GAME "Accordingly, we inform you that the match between the two clubs, originally scheduled for this Sunday, October 25, has been postponed to Monday, October 26, at 8:30 p.m. at the Parc des Princes," the club said in a statement. The Paris police requested the change because police and security resources are stretched thin due to mass protests, ongoing civil unrest, and France's first NFL game happening in the region, per multiple reports. EXCLUSIVE: SECRETARY OF STATE MARCO RUBIO GIVES NFL COMMISSIONER ASSURANCES THAT GAME IN FRANCE 'WILL BE FINE' That NFL game remains as scheduled on Sunday starting at 9:30 a.m. in the United States. The NFL said so in reply to an email from OutKick and Fox News Digital asking whether and how its decision to play on Sunday is impacted by the decision by PSG. It's not. And that is quite clear considering NFL elites and the French government expect the game to go on. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, Saints owner Gayle Benson and Steelers owner Art Rooney II met with French President Emmanuel Macron for a luncheon meeting Friday at the Élysée Palace in Paris. According to a league source, the topics discussed at the two-hour gathering included security for the game, the readiness of the Stade de France, where the game is to be played, and the growth of flag football in France. The fact the French President met with the highest representatives from both squads and there has been no change in the status of the game suggests this thing is going to happen come heck or high rioting. And on that front, it seems Saturday is a key day because protests which may or may not evolve into wider civil unrest are planned for that day. Organizers of the Paris protest told the Associated Press that an administrative court overturned a protest ban issued by police after they challenged it. The Paris prefecture previously said the ban was necessary, given the risk of street violence after groups of masked youth clashed with officers, looted shops and torched cars over the weekend. The organizers signed a police document stating that the protest would remain stationary due to the risk of violence. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! More bans were expected in the coming days. Macron previously said ban measures aim to protect city centers, businesses and public buildings. Macron said after a special security meeting at the Elysée Palace that the strategy adopted for the coming days is to ban protests requested by "individuals or groups with no legitimate authority." "The rules are simple, and I think they’re just common sense. The general recommendation is that there should be no demonstrations in the coming days," he said. "For those who still want to protest, if they are trade unions, prefects will propose alternative routes." Macron blamed last weekend's violence on "actions led by radical far-left groups who aimed to bring the Republic down," in addition to criminals who came to loot. articles.title: Knicks' Jalen Brunson Reportedly Will Join Peyton, Eli Manning's 'ManningCast' for Eagles-Cowboys
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson will be a guest on the ManningCast featuring Peyton and Eli Manning for a Week 7 matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys, according to Jared Schwartz of the New York Post.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson will be a guest on the ManningCast featuring Peyton and Eli Manning for a Week 7 matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys, according to Jared Schwartz of the New York Post .

Per Schwartz, Brunson is set to make an appearance on ESPN's alternate broadcast during the third quarter of the game.

While the three-time All-Star helped the Knicks end a 53-year championship drought last season, he's a noted Eagles fan.

Brunson was stellar throughout New York's 2026 playoff run, averaging a league-leading 28.4 points per game on 46.5/36.3/84.6 shooting splits. He earned Eastern Conference Finals MVP honors before taking home the Finals MVP award.

As for Monday's NFC East clash, the Eagles and Cowboys are both looking to put slow starts behind them.

Philadelphia sits at just 2-4, as its outlook for the remainder of the year is murky with quarterback Jalen Hurts set to miss the rest of the season due to a blood clot diagnosis.

Dallas similarly owns a 2-4 record, suffering losses in three of its past four games.

Kickoff between the Eagles and Cowboys is on Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Fans are sick and tired of the NFL's obsession with flags, anthem fatigue is real & UGA football is too smart!
articles.summary: NFL penalty frustrations and national anthem fatigue dominate fan reactions as the World Series, Brewers, and college football take center stage.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news, and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. We're eight days out, folks. Eight days away from Halloween. Hard to believe, right? October is flying by, and for good reason. We've got a TON going on right now — and that doesn't even include the World Series, which starts tonight. Show of hands ... who's paying attention? I know there's this big debate about small market teams and lack of interest ... blah, blah, blah. RAYS PUNCH THEIR TICKET TO THE WORLD SERIES, TAKING DOWN GUARDIANS IN GAME 6 TO SET UP SERIES WITH BREWERS I don't care. Anything — and I mean anything — beats having to watch the Dodgers. Give me some fresh blood in the Fall Classic. I don't even like the Rays, but I'll take them over the alternative. Obviously, we're all rooting for the Brewers, right? Feels like that's a pretty unanimous choice. If you haven't watched a single second of Brewers baseball this year, do me a favor and watch the first inning tonight. BREWERS' FLAMETHROWER JACOB MISIOROWSKI LIGHTS UP RECORD BOOKS WITH TRIPLE-DIGIT SPEEDS IN GEM VS YANKEES Wait till you see this Jacob Misiorowski pitch. He's gonna blow your minds. On that note, welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where fans (you guys!) weigh in on two things that are pretty top-of-mind at the moment ... Penalties in the NFL, and the ongoing anthem controversies in both the W and NBA. Spoiler alert: You're sick of both! I don't blame you. What else? I've got bedlam in Boone, I thought Kirk Herbstreit was actually really good alongside Al Michaels last night (see, I can be nice!), and let's check in with UGA fans after last week's horrible loss to Auburn. They're doing great! OK, grab you some bologna for National Bologna Day, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap! Frustrated fans, Part I! I'm certain we've celebrated this day before, because I contend that bologna is one of the more — if not the most — underrated meats on the market. People dunk on bologna all the time, and it's baffling to me. I don't get it. I'd put a fried bologna sammy over any sammy in this country. I'm dead serious. It's rare that you can find one anymore, but if you do, you're in for quite a ride. Nice thick slice of bologna? Cheese? Toasted bun. The best. Mount Rushmore of deli meats? Sure! Why not? 1. Bologna (duh) 2. Pepperoni (not sure it counts as a deli meat, but I get it from my Publix deli, so it counts today) 3. Turkey (gotta be sandwich-sliced though. If it's too thin, I walk away. Thinly sliced turkey is for the birds) 4. Roast beef (I had chicken in this spot last year, but I've evolved) And that concludes our culinary portion of today's class! Gordon Ramsay would be proud. OK, let's go ahead and get started by addressing some fan frustration from this past week. First, we'll start with last night's flag-fest in Chicago: Frustrated fans, Part II! Yikes. Look, I don't even think last night was that bad when you compare it to the rest of the year, but still ... the flags in the NFL are out of control right now. I believe Al Michaels made a comment about it last night. Whenever there's a big play, you almost expect a flag. You're STUNNED when you don't see one. That's not a great place to be. There's no flow in these games anymore. No rhythm. It's just a three-hour ref show at this point. I don't know who to blame, by the way. The players? The coaches? The league for, at times, forgetting it's actually tackle football? Everyone probably shares some of it. Bottom line? It's hurting the product. Something has to change. Moving on ... Yesterday, I asked the class how y'all felt about the ongoing anthem debates raging in both the WNBA and with LeBron James. I was curious, mainly because I'm personally just over it all. I don't care anymore. I think it's all silly and the players doing it are insufferable, but I'm just tired of giving them oxygen at this point. It's not worth it. You guys agreed. Here's a quick sampling of some of the responses I received — and I received DOZENS of emails last night. Herbie, Boone & UGA's GPA! Yeah, I cannot stand LeBron James. He's awful, and has been for decades now. He's the worst. But it's 2026. We've known this about LeBron for YEARS now. Why should I let it bother me anymore? What's the point? Why am I letting LEBRON JAMES or the WNBA girls affect my mood? It's silly. I'm over it. Most of you are, too. OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL. First up? I give Herbie and Al Michaels a lot of grief, but I thought Kirk was actually really good last night. He absolutely nailed the most pivotal moment of the game: I was screaming at the TV the second I saw it happen. That play was straight out of the Bill Belichick handbook. I thought it was actually brilliant by Mike Vrabel, and I'm no Mike Vrabel fan. It's the right call. If you somehow stop them, you have to waste a timeout. That's one. They're gonna go for it because Ben Johnson is Ben Johnson. The chances of getting another stop on 4th and inches are very slim. If you don't, the game is basically over because you're only going to have one timeout left and they'll have a new set of downs. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE I'd take my chances with the 58-yard field goal any day of the week in that spot. Good work, Herbie! Less of the dog, and more of THAT! Next? While everyone was watching that Bears-Pats ending, I was dialed in on the App. State-JMU game over in Boone. And buddy, it was college football at its finest: THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! I mean, it's just the best. This season, more than any other I can remember, has really separated college and the NFL for me. Right now, college football is clearly No. 1 and it's not particularly close. It's just a better all-around product at the moment, and the gap is getting wider by the week. OK, that's it for today. Good class, everyone. While we're talking some college football, I leave you with this incredible message board regarding the University of Georgia football team. articles.title: Falcons' throwback logo will not feature stripes from viral social media post
articles.summary: Atlanta's post about its throwback logo drew jokes and criticism about its similarity to Nazi symbolism.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons will take the field Sunday with a throwback logo on their helmets — but not the design that went viral.

As part of their throwback uniforms, the Falcons will bring back a black falcon logo that the team used for more than four decades, starting in the 1960s.

To promote the throwbacks, Atlanta made a social media post showing the design, captioning that it was the team's new profile picture. The post incorporated the throwback logo with a background of red with black, gold and cream stripes, which mimics the striping on the team's retro helmets.

But people online quickly pointed out how the combination of the colors and the black logo evoked the Nazi flag, leading to satirical jokes.

The post is still up on the Falcons' social media, but is no longer the team's profile picture; that change appeared to take place Thursday, after the initial social media reaction. The new profile picture shows a helmet with the retro logo, but without the striping.

The Falcons declined to comment to ESPN about the issue, and the NFL did not respond to a request for comment from the Associated Press .

Atlanta will wear the throwback logos as they host the San Francisco 49ers for Week 7.

articles.title: Trevon Diggs Released by Seahawks, Latest NFL Rumors Update Buzz on CB's Future
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks released cornerback Trevon Diggs on Friday, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks released cornerback Trevon Diggs on Friday, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram .

According to Gregg Bell of 93.3 KJR, the Seahawks released Diggs to free up space on their 53-man roster in order for guard Anthony Bradford to come off injured reserve and suit up against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7.

Seattle will likely seek to bring back Diggs on its practice squad, per Bell.

The 28-year-old has appeared in three games for the Seahawks this season.

Diggs initially signed with Seattle as a free agent on Aug. 19, although he wasn't able to earn a spot on the team's 53-man roster at the end of training camp. He was retained on the Seahawks' practice squad instead.

On Oct. 10, Seattle signed Diggs off its practice squad ahead of a Week 5 clash with the San Francisco 49ers.

In his three regular-season appearances, he recorded one tackle. He also allowed a 91.7 passer rating when targeted in coverage, according to Pro Football Focus .

Diggs' NFL career started on a high note with the Dallas Cowboys, as he earned Pro Bowl recognition in two consecutive seasons from 2021-22. During his 2021 campaign, he racked up a league-leading 11 interceptions.

Health issues started to impact Diggs, as he suffered a torn ACL in 2023 before missing time during his 2025 season due to a concussion .

While he wasn't able to keep his 53-man roster spot as part of a deep Seahawks secondary, it appears as though he could return to the practice squad of the defending Super Bowl champions.

Seattle has opened this season with a 3-3 record.

articles.title: Craig Carton explains why the NFL has some questions to ask after bizarre moment in Bears-Patriots game
articles.summary: Craig Carton questions why Chicago Bears DB Malik Muhammad ran away from Rhamondre Stevenson on a late touchdown, demanding an NFL investigation.
articles.body: Sports betting is a big part of the sports experience these days, and unfortunately, that will lead to questions about the game's integrity, as OutKick's Craig Carton pointed out on Friday's edition of "The Craig Carton Show." The Chicago Bears took on the New England Patriots on Thursday, and there was a certain play late in the first half that caught Carton's attention. Patriots running back Rhamondre Stephenson caught a screen pass at midfield and somehow took it all the way to the house for a late touchdown with no time left on the clock. But it was what Bears DB Malik Muhammad did on the play that had Carton asking questions. RHAMONDRE STEVENSON'S MIRACULOUS 48-YARD TOUCHDOWN STUNS BEARS AS CLOCK EXPIRES IN FIRST HALF Did... did Muhammad turn and run in the complete opposite direction that Stephenson was headed? Well, it's at least worth asking some questions. NBA AND MANY SPORTSBOOKS AGREE TO BAN MULTIPLE TYPES OF BETS DUE TO RECENT BETTING SCANDALS "What Malik Muhammad does next is why every single person that is against legalized wagering thinks the fix is in," he said. "Rather than step into the hole and make an attempt to tackle Stevenson, he literally runs away from the play." Whether it was a bad read or something else, there's really no question: that was about as big a whiff as you'll see in the NFL. Fortunately, that play didn't have any impact on the game as the Bears won and covered the spread. Carton noted that the play likely got more attention because it was on a Thursday night, and that the NFL should be asking some questions. "And that's the type of play that needs to be investigated," he said. "The NFL now has to sit down and interview Malik Muhammad and interview Ben Johnson of the Bears and get an explanation as to why (Muhammad was) running away from the ball carrier? Like it makes no sense at all. There's not even a logical, reasonable explanation of 'Well, I was going this way because I thought he might cut outside.' CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "No, there was no chance to cut outside because by you coming this way, you opened up a seven-yard gap."

articles.title: Lawrence McCutcheon Dies at 76 After Parkinson's Diagnosis, Rams Legend Made 5 Pro Bowls
articles.summary: Former Los Angeles Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon, a five-time Pro Bowler who amassed four 1,000-yard seasons, has died at the age of 76 after a lengthy battle with Parkinson's disease.
articles.body:
Former Los Angeles Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon, a five-time Pro Bowler who amassed four 1,000-yard seasons, has died at the age of 76 after a lengthy battle with Parkinson's disease.

The McCutcheon family revealed news of his passing via a statement, which the Rams shared on Friday.

NFL legend announces Parkinson's diagnosis

McCutcheon also served as the Rams' director of player personnel from 2003-2016.

articles.title: Mike Evans Injured, Latest Updates on 49ers Star's Achilles and Status for Falcons Game
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers will be without receiver Mike Evans, among others, for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers will be without receiver Mike Evans, among others, for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.

Evans missed the end of Monday's win over the Washington Commanders with an Achilles injury. He limped to the locker room shortly before halftime and was ruled out following intermission.

After the game, head coach Kyle Shanahan downplayed the injury:

Evans had an injury designation of Achilles and ribs coming into the game, but the 49ers announced he was active prior to kickoff.

He will now miss Sunday's contest, which comes right before a Week bye.

The veteran was having an excellent game prior to the setback with three catches for 94 yards, 54 of which came on a single reception. It was more of the same after he dominated his last game against the Seattle Seahawks with seven catches for 113 yards and one touchdown.

Evans arrived in San Francisco this offseason after establishing himself as a franchise legend for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The No. 7 overall pick of the 2014 NFL draft surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first 11 years in the league. He was also a six-time Pro Bowler during that span and is one of the best players in Tampa Bay history.

However, injuries limited him to just eight games last season, which snapped his streak.

Evans' health is now under the microscope again following Monday's setback.

Wide receiver was already a position of concern for the 49ers even before this injury, as Deebo Samuel was sidelined against the Commanders. Ricky Pearsall is also out for the season, while De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are sidelined as well.

While the team can rely on running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle, it will be up to players such as Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing to produce if Evans is out for an extended amount of time.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's $1.7 billion Cleveland Guardians investment reveals his deep-rooted hometown loyalty
articles.summary: Travis Kelce may have built his legacy in Kansas City, but his sporting heart still belongs to Cleveland.
articles.body: Travis Kelce may have built his legacy in Kansas City, but his sporting heart still belongs to Cleveland. The three-time Super Bowl champion has never forgotten the baseball memories that shaped his childhood in Northeast Ohio. Now, his connection to the Cleveland Guardians carries greater meaning after he joined the franchise's ownership group in May 2026. His latest comments about Cleveland's baseball culture reveal why the city means so much to him. For Kelce, baseball is not just another sport. It is a family tradition, a childhood passion and a lasting link to home.Travis Kelce reveals why Cleveland remains a baseball townKelce's love for Cleveland baseball began long before he became an NFL superstar. Growing up during the 1990s, he watched a team that regularly competed for American League honours and captured the city's imagination.Stars such as Kenny Lofton, Carlos Baerga, Jim Thome and Sandy Alomar Jr. helped make those teams memorable. Their performances gave young fans plenty of reasons to follow the franchise, while postseason appearances turned baseball into a shared community experience.Kelce has also spoken about the simple rituals that made those days special. Trips downtown with his father, rides on Cleveland's rapid transit system and keeping score at the ballpark helped turn his interest into a lifelong attachment.Speaking on the New Heights podcast, Kelce described Cleveland as a baseball town, reflecting on the city's longstanding desire to see its team succeed in October.His comments do not diminish Cleveland's passionate football following. The Browns remain central to the city's sporting culture, while the Cavaliers brought home an NBA championship in 2016. However, baseball holds a distinct place in Kelce's childhood memories.That emotional connection helps explain why his loyalty has survived years of playing professional football elsewhere.Cleveland Guardians' 2026 playoff run strengthened Travis Kelce's connectionThe Guardians gave their supporters plenty to celebrate during the 2026 postseason. Cleveland recovered from a two-game deficit against the Chicago White Sox in the American League Division Series, winning three straight elimination games to advance.José Ramírez delivered the decisive blow in Game 5 with a two-run home run in a 2-0 victory. Cleveland then carried that momentum into the American League Championship Series against the Tampa Bay Rays.However, the run ended in disappointment. Tampa Bay won the series in six games, securing a 7-3 victory on October 19.Despite the exit, Cleveland's comeback reinforced the bond between the team and its supporters. For a city that has endured decades of championship heartbreak, every deep postseason run brings renewed hope.Kelce's connection now extends beyond childhood memories. His minority investment in the Guardians, announced in May 2026, gives him a direct stake in the franchise's future.Although his NFL career remains tied to the Kansas City Chiefs, his involvement with Cleveland shows that professional success has not erased his hometown loyalty. For Kelce, the Guardians represent more than a baseball team. They are part of the sporting history that shaped him long before the world knew his name.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dak Prescott Talks Cowboys Mindset for Eagles Game Amid 2-4 Start to NFL Season
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott detailed the team's approach to a Week 7 clash with the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott detailed the team's approach to a Week 7 clash with the Philadelphia Eagles.

Prescott explained that the Cowboys' mindset is "determined, and I would hope urgent," according to ESPN's Todd Archer .

"We can only say we've got a lot of games in front of us for so long. Might be already past us, right? We've got to go win," Prescott said. "You've got to go win. You want to give yourself a chance to be a winning team, to be a playoff team. You got to win as many games as you can, and when you drop two games -- in particular games that we didn't expect to drop -- it makes it that much harder. So urgent, urgent to get it done now."

Schottenheimer 'Pissed Off' by Cowboys Start

The Cowboys have opened the year with a 2-4 record, with three losses coming in their past four games.

Dallas' defense has continued to struggle, giving up at least 28 points in three of the team's six contests. The Cowboys are also allowing 382.5 total yards per game, ranking No. 30 in the NFL.

Prescott has started all six games for Dallas this season, completing 66.3 percent of his throws for 1,639 yards and 10 touchdowns compared to five interceptions.

Despite the Cowboys' slow start, they can still turn their season around and contend in the NFC East.

The New York Giants sit atop the division standings at 3-2-1, although J.J. McCarthy is set to become the team's third starting quarterback this year.

The Eagles are tied with Dallas at 2-4, but they're dealing with uncertainty under center after Jalen Hurts was ruled out for the remainder of the year following a blood clot diagnosis.

Dallas and Philadelphia will face off on Monday night, with kickoff at 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Vance receives warm reception during Bengals visit despite negative media portrayal: source
articles.summary: Video from JD Vance's Cincinnati Bengals practice visit tells a different story than the viral clip, showing handshakes with coach Zac Taylor.
articles.body: The narrative on social media that Vice President JD Vance was ignored by multiple Cincinnati Bengals players at a recent team practice apparently does not reflect what actually unfolded that day, a source with knowledge of the visit told OutKick. A recent video shared online showed Vance and his family outside the team's locker room on Thursday as the team walked back in. The video, that did not have clear audio of the interaction, showed Bengals tight end Drew Sample stop to shake the vice president's hand as other players walked by. But footage obtained by OutKick portrayed a different story, including a handshake with an enthusiastic Bengals head coach Zac Taylor. The video also captured audio and appeared to show Vance chopping it up with players and other staffers. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Seeing how the media works is actually pretty crazy. The players, staff, and Vice President Vance and his son all had a great time at practice," the source told OutKick exclusively. "All of these negative tweets and articles are completely detached from the reality of how well the visit went." Initial reaction to the video shared on social described the interaction as Vance getting "snubbed" by the team. "This is what TOTAL HUMILIATION looks like: JD Vance attempted to greet Cincinnati Bengals players in the locker room and got snubbed and ghosted by every single player except one," one person wrote on X. "JD Vance walked into the Bengals locker room looking for a photo-op, and the players gave him the cold shoulder he deserves," another person wrote, adding that the team didn't want to be used for"political theater." But the source told OutKick that Vance and his son were warmly received when visiting the facility with no planned media engagement. A photo obtained by OutKick showed the vice president and his family playing catch on the field. The source added that defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence approached the vice president and had conversation with him during the visit. TITANS PLAYER WHO GOT INTO ARGUMENT THAT PROVOKED 'UNFORTUNATE' GUN INCIDENT SPEAKS OUT Vance, an Ohio native, is a longtime Bengals fan, growing up roughly an hour outside of Cincinnati. He has a home in Cincinnati’s East Walnut Hills neighborhood. Vance toured the team's locker room, shook hands with several players, coach Zac Taylor and others, and came away with a football. It is unclear if Vance brought the ball to be autographed or the club gave it to him as a memento. Quarterback Joe Burrow said he "did not" talk to Vance. "He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn't get to," Burrow told reporters earlier this week. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Vance was in town to deliver a speech at the FBI's Cincinnati Field Office and then hold a campaign rally at the Sharonville Convention Center. OutKick's Armando Salguero contributed to this report.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders unionize, to start collective bargaining after pushing for better wages for years
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys agreed to recognize the newly formed union as the collective bargaining representative for the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, one of the most famous dance groups in sports — let alone the country — have unionized after their limited pay and benefits have been the subject of discussion and controversy for years.

And their newly formed union is now recognized by the Dallas Cowboys as the collective bargaining representative for the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.

The union, officially named the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association (DCCA), gained that recognition "after meaningful discussion" with the Cowboys, according to a Friday news release from the parties , which states that they are set to start collective bargaining.

During Season 2 of the Netflix docuseries "America's Sweethearts" — one of the multiple television series that have profiled the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders — the dancers' salaries were thrust back into the spotlight.

The cheerleaders said they were due to receive a 400% pay raise for the 2025 season, as reported by The Dallas Morning News .

While the show didn't disclose the new wages, or detail the cheerleaders' previous earnings, Jada McLean told The New York Teams that she was making $15 an hour and $500 for each appearance in 2024, her fifth and final year with the squad (compensation varies by experience, she explained).

After the raise that was revealed in Season 2 of "America's Sweethearts," though, veteran cheerleaders could be reeling in more than $75 an hour, McLean told the Times. That new contract, according to the June 2025 report from the Times , altered the pay structure for game days and other appearances as well, except it still didn't provide health insurance, per McLean.

Back in 2018, Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Erica Wilkins filed a federal fair wage lawsuit against the Cowboys, whom Forbes values at $17 billion . Wilkins, according to The Guardian , claimed she averaged $15,000 during her seasons and brought in less money than the Cowboys' male mascot.

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have been a staple for decades. Their high kicks are iconic, as is their "Thunderstruck" routine.

The group surged in popularity among a new generation of fans when Netflix debuted "America's Sweethearts" in 2024. There have now been three seasons of that show.

Time will tell if, or how much, impending collective bargaining between DCCA and the Cowboys will improve the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' compensation.

It's worth noting that, in 1995, the Buffalo Bills' cheerleaders won a National Labor Relations Board ruling that allowed them to unionize, per the Associated Press via the Los Angeles Times . It was also reported at the time that the group, the Buffalo Jills, then joined the National Football League Cheerleaders Association.

That was reportedly the first union to represent a professional cheerleading squad. The union didn't last, however, and the Jills suspended operations in 2014 in the wake of a lawsuit filed by former cheerleaders who, per ESPN , claimed they were underpaid and mistreated.

articles.title: Giants linebacker Tremaine Edmunds out for remainder of 2026 season with shoulder injury
articles.summary: Edmunds suffered the injury attempting to make a tackle late in Week 6's loss to the Saints. He was the Giants' leading tackler in their first six games.
articles.body:
New York Giants linebacker Tremaine Edmunds will miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a shoulder injury, The Athletic's Dan Duggan reports .

Edmunds was already listed as out for Week 7's matchup with the Houston Texans. However, he is apparently dealing with a torn muscle extending to his chest, according to ESPN's Jordan Ranaan .

The injury occurred late in the Giants' 34-27 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 6. Reaching with his left arm attempting to tackle Saints running back Kendre Miller, Edmunds stayed down on the field after the play.

Edmunds, 28, was in his first season with the Giants. He signed a three-year, $36 million deal in March, days after the Chicago Bears released him to create $15 million in salary cap space.

In six games, Edmunds compiled 50 total tackles with 2 sacks and 3 tackles for loss as the Giants' defensive playcaller. He appeared to be on his way to a ninth consecutive season recording 100 or more tackles, averaging 129 per year.

Edmunds was a Pro Bowl selection in 2019 and 2020 with the Buffalo Bills, who made him their 2018 first-round pick (No. 16 overall) out of Virginia Tech.

Micah McFadden is expected to replace Edmunds at one of the Giants' inside linebacker spots alongside rookie (and first-round pick) Arvell Reese. McFadden, 26, has appeared in five games this season, recording 4 tackles. He started at inside linebacker in 2023 and 2024, averaging 104 tackles per season.

Edmunds' injury further erodes the Giants' depth at linebacker. Edge rusher Chauncey Golsteon will also miss the remainder of the season with a neck injury. Fellow edge Brian Burns tore his ACL in Week 3's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
